title: Microprocessor Interfacing
description: Microcomputers and microprocessors, embedded systems and microcontrollers, the Intel 8085, interfacing memory and I/O and the 8255, the 8259A interrupt controller and 8257 DMA controller, the 8086 and the 8051. Built from the CSC 412 course material by Adebola K. Ojo, the case-study slides and the 2022/23 examination.

topics.title: Microcomputer and Microprocessor Basics
topics.summary: A microcomputer has input, memory, processor (ALU and control unit) and output units, organized in a von Neumann or Harvard architecture. A microprocessor is a single-chip VLSI CPU, made in technologies such as TTL, ECL and CMOS, classified by word length and by instruction set (CISC, RISC, VLIW, superscalar), and chosen by factors such as word size and speed.
subtopics: Types and basic blocks of a microcomputer
Computer architecture: ISA, microarchitecture, system design
What a microprocessor is: bit, word, address, data and control buses
CISC, RISC, VLIW and superscalar; selection factors

topics.title: Embedded Systems and Microcontrollers
topics.summary: An embedded system is a computer designed for specific control functions within a larger system, running firmware from ROM or flash with limited resources. A microcontroller is a processor with on-chip memory and peripherals that works as a standalone system, whereas a microprocessor needs external memory and peripherals but offers more computing power.
subtopics: Characteristics: dedicated task, real-time constraints, firmware
User interfaces and applications of embedded systems
Memory in embedded systems: ROM, flash and RAM

topics.title: The Intel 8085 Microprocessor
topics.summary: The 8085 is an 8-bit, 40-pin microprocessor with a 16-bit address bus (64 KB), an accumulator, six general-purpose registers, a flag register (S, Z, AC, P, CY), and 16-bit program counter and stack pointer. Its instructions are classified by function and by length, it has four addressing modes, and five hardware interrupts with TRAP the highest priority.
subtopics: Program counter, stack pointer and buses; ALE, RD, WR, IO/M, S1 and S0
Instructions by function and by length (one-, two-, three-byte)
Interrupts: TRAP, RST 7.5, 6.5, 5.5 and INTR; RST instructions

topics.title: Interfacing Memory and I/O with the 8085
topics.summary: Memory chips are interfaced to the 8085 through address decoders (NAND gates or the 74LS138), and I/O devices are interfaced either as peripheral-mapped (I/O-mapped) I/O or as memory-mapped I/O. The 8255 Programmable Peripheral Interface provides three 8-bit ports in two groups, programmed by a control word in modes 0, 1 and 2.
subtopics: Interfacing memory chips with address decoders
The 8255: ports A, B and C; groups A and B

topics.title: The 8259A Interrupt Controller and 8257 DMA Controller
topics.summary: The 8259A Programmable Interrupt Controller handles eight prioritized, maskable interrupts and can be cascaded to 64. Direct memory access transfers data between a device and memory without the CPU; the 8257 is a four-channel DMA controller that requests the bus with HOLD and starts after HLDA.
subtopics: The 8259A: eight interrupts, vectoring and priority
What DMA is and why it is fastest
HOLD and HLDA; DMA read, write and verify cycles
The 8257: four channels, address and terminal count registers
Mode set register; DMA modes of operation

topics.title: The Intel 8086 Microprocessor
topics.summary: The 8086 is a 16-bit microprocessor with a 20-bit address bus (1 MB), divided into a Bus Interface Unit that prefetches up to six instruction bytes and an Execution Unit that executes them, which pipelines fetch and execution. It uses segmented memory, eight addressing modes, and works in minimum (single-processor) or maximum (multiprocessor) mode.

topics.title: The Intel 8051 Microcontroller
topics.summary: The 8051 is an 8-bit microcontroller with 4 KB of on-chip ROM, four register banks, four I/O ports, two 16-bit timers and a serial port. Its timers are configured with TMOD and TCON, delays are computed from the 1.085 µs machine cycle at 11.0592 MHz, and serial data uses SCON and SBUF.
subtopics: Ports P0–P3 and the EA pin
Programming Timer 0 in mode 1; delay calculation
